explanation:
[EFFECT]
The hour of day has a strongly non-monotonic, bimodal effect on predicted demand. Contributions are deeply negative in the early morning hours (roughly midnight to 5 am), reaching their lowest point at 4 am, meaning demand is multiplied well below its baseline during those hours. Demand then rises sharply through the morning, peaking at 8 am (the morning commute), dips slightly through midday, and then climbs to its overall highest point at 5 pm (the evening commute), before gradually declining back through the evening into negative territory after 11 pm.

[IMPORTANCE]
Hour of day is the single most important feature in the model, ranked 1st out of 9 features, with an importance score (0.89) that is substantially larger than any other feature. It drives the widest swings in predicted demand of anything the model considers.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Bike availability and staff levels should be concentrated around the two commuter peaks — approximately 7–9 am and 4–7 pm on weekdays — and sharply reduced during the early morning hours (roughly 1–5 am), when the model predicts demand to be a fraction of the daily average.
